subject: Request: Interim SLA reprieve and burst credit offer for Acme AI
messages:
From: Jill Park <jill.park@acme.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-26T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Increased tail latency impacting inference pipelines

Hi Rishi,

We're seeing repeated tail-latency spikes on the Redwood endpoint that runs our real-time scoring. Between 2026-11-24 22:00 and 2026-11-25 04:30 UTC we've had multiple 99.9th-percentile spikes above 3.5s which is outside the SLO in our contract. This has caused 7 downstream job timeouts and some customer-impact on our side.

Can you advise on a path to temporary relief ahead of our renewal conversation next month? Specifically, we'd like a short-term commercial gesture (billing allowance or a burst credit) while you complete the incident RCA and mitigation plan. I'm attaching the logs and our token usage extract.

Attachments: acme-incident-1126.log; usage-breakdown-nov.csv

Thanks,
Jill Park
Head of Platform
Acme AI

Looping you both in — Jill from Acme escalated production tail latency. They attached logs and a usage CSV (see thread below). Can ops confirm: 1) incident window and root cause summary; 2) recommended commercial remediation (amount/format) we can offer quickly; 3) whether a burst token allocation is technically feasible for Dec billing cycle.

Marissa — after ops' rec, I need a commercial proposal to present to Karthik for exec sign-off (we can include Finance later). Please prepare the wording (credit %, duration, any caveats).

Target: get an interim offer to Acme within 48 hours so they have something ahead of renewal.

Thanks,

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-27T11:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Increased tail latency impacting inference pipelines

Thanks for the ping. Quick summary from SRE side:
- Incident window confirmed: 2026-11-24 22:15 UTC -> 2026-11-25 03:20 UTC.
- Root cause: transient NVMe I/O contention on a subset of hosts during a batch maintenance job, which increased kernel scheduling jitter and delayed KV cache population for a small shard group. This primarily affected requests with long prompt prefixes (our 95-99.9th).
- Remediation: ops fixed the batch maintenance scheduling and evicted affected shard caches; we've applied a safety throttle for those hosts. Full patch (kernel tuning + scheduler guardrails) is scheduled for 2026-12-04.

Commercial suggestion (recommended):
- Tiered allowance: 
  1) One-time invoice credit = 10% of November net usage charges (covers measurable billing impact and customer goodwill)
  2) Burst credit = 200,000 free token-equivalents applied to December billing window to offset engineering reruns and Q4 load testing.
  3) A conditional clause that credits are one-time and do not set precedence for recurring outages; include a short RCA packet and mitigation timeline.

I've attached a two-page incident summary and the usage breakdown we generated for Acme.

Attachments: incident-summary-1126.pdf; usage-breakdown-nov.csv

If you want to be conservative on $ impact, we can convert the burst credit to a $ amount instead.

Lauren Bishop
Head of Cloud Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Exec sign-off request: interim SLA allowance for Acme AI (DEAL-ACME-3421)

Karthik / Marissa —

Acme (DEAL-ACME-3421) reported multiple tail-latency spikes over 11/24-11/25 that impacted their real-time scoring jobs. Ops provided an RCA and recommended we offer a small commercial gesture to keep the renewal conversation constructive. Summary of proposal below:

Proposal (ops recommended):
- One-time invoice credit = 10% of November net usage charges (estimated $14.5k)
- Burst credit = 200k token-equivalents usable in Dec 2026 (tokens applied at per-token rate in invoice)
- Requirement: we deliver RCA + a mitigation timeline; credits applied after acceptance of terms and an acknowledgement from Acme that credits are one-time.

Rationale: short-term commercial relief reduces renewal friction, cost impact is predictable and limited (estimated $14.5k + marginal token cost), and ops' patch schedule reduces risk going into December.

Request: Exec approval to commit the above offer and go live with customer communication. If approved, I'll draft the email to Acme and copy Finance for tracking.

Relevant links: JIRA-INC-9876, incident-summary-1126.pdf, HubSpot: hs_record_54921

--
Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0132

Subject: Re: Exec sign-off request: interim SLA allowance for Acme AI (DEAL-ACME-3421)

Approved with conditions — thanks for the concise packet.

Conditions:
1) Finance (Monica) must confirm the exact invoice line items and GL coding for the 10% credit (Monica, please confirm).
2) Rishi: raise JIRA-INC-9876 as a customer-facing incident with the RCA attached and mark the mitigation due date (2026-12-04) so the CS team can reference it in the renewal motion.
3) Marissa: prepare a short customer email (I prefer the tone to be constructive + show value: what we fixed, what we'll do, and the one-time goodwill offer).
4) The burst credit should be tracked as a non-monetary ledger item against the account and expire 2026-12-31 if unused.

Once Finance confirms ledger treatment, action and notify Acme. Keep the legal/corporate terms minimal — a one-paragraph acknowledgement is enough.

Karthik
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
